bullets.title: NVDA: $500B AI financing deal with Wall Street giants; stock drops ~3%
bullets.body: NVIDIA confirmed MOUs with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to mobilize over $500B of third-party capital for AI infrastructure financing. Despite the scale of the announcement, NVDA shares fell ~3% to session lows on the day, with some critics characterizing the deal as masking limited FCF. Unusual $3M+ call prints were also noted in NVDA options tape.

bullets.title: AAPL: Jefferies downgrades to Underperform on iPhone roadmap concerns; CXMT chip testing reported
bullets.body: Jefferies cut Apple to Underperform from Hold with a $263.66 PT, citing a challenging path to higher-priced iPhones including cancellation of the planned all-glass iPhone (scrapped due to poor yields; was expected at ~$2,600 ASP in Sept 2027). Separately, Apple is testing CXMT Chinese DRAM chips for iPhone and MacBook, adding supply chain/geopolitical complexity. Shares fell 2.5%.

bullets.title: INTC: $15B equity offering, multiple times oversubscribed; stock down ~4-5%
bullets.body: Intel launched a $15B common stock secondary offering (underwritten by JPMorgan, Goldman, Morgan Stanley, Citi) to fund AI compute capacity expansion, including capex guidance raised to ~$20B. The offering was multiple times oversubscribed despite shares falling 4-5%. Intel also secured customer commitments for its 14A node process.

bullets.title: TTD: Multiple downgrades across sell-side (BNP to Underperform, DA Davidson to Neutral, HSBC to Reduce)
bullets.body: Trade Desk was cut to Underperform at BNP Paribas Exane (PT to $10 from $22, implying 23% downside), to Neutral at DA Davidson, and to Reduce at HSBC, with the consensus concern being Q3 guidance implying the first year-over-year revenue decline since going public.

bullets.title: NFLX: Nearly doubles US upfront ad commitments; CFO sells 9.2K shares
bullets.body: Netflix doubled its US upfront ad sales commitments and is on track for $3B in ad revenue in 2026. Shares rallied ~2.9% on the session. Separately, CFO Spencer Neumann sold 9.2K shares at $76.29 via Form 4, retaining 73.8K shares.

bullets.title: META +2%: Muse Glimmer open-weights release and free/affordable AI plans
bullets.body: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30B parameter model optimized for single consumer GPU deployment, and plans to release weights for the more powerful Muse Spark model. Shares rose ~2.1% to a two-week high. CEO open-source strategy seen as major competitive move vs. OpenAI/Anthropic. Additionally, appeals court allowed 3,000+ addiction lawsuits against Meta (and Google) to proceed.

bullets.title: MSFT: Maia 300 AI chip to be unveiled in September; targeting ~1M unit production
bullets.body: Microsoft plans to unveil its next-generation Maia 300 AI chip in September, aiming for roughly 1 million units but constrained by TSMC capacity. The company is also in discussions with TSMC for next-gen production of custom chips and is ramping AI chip efforts to reduce reliance on NVDA.

bullets.title: TSM: July revenue +45% YoY to $14.5B; FY guidance raised above 40% growth
bullets.body: TSMC reported July revenue of NT$467.58B (~$14.5B), up ~45% year-over-year on AI chip demand. Revenue for the first seven months reached $89.1B (+37% YoY), with full-year growth now expected above 40%. TSM and Sony are also forming a ¥1 trillion joint venture in Kumamoto for next-gen chip production.

bullets.title: MU: KeyBanc raises PT to $1,750 at KBCM TLF; demand outstripping supply into 2027
bullets.body: KeyBanc maintains Overweight with $1,750 PT (9x FY27 EPS of $189.62). Key takeaways: MU cannot meet half of datacenter customer demand; SCAs now cover ~50% of revenue with multi-year take-or-pay contracts through CY30; custom HBM (HBM4E+) shifts memory toward ASIC-like single/dual-sourcing model with premium pricing; physical AI (humanoids) seen as next major demand driver. Memory expected at 42% of iPhone 18 Pro BoM and 62% of NVDA Vera Rubin BoM.

bullets.title: SNDK: Upgraded to Buy at Argus Research, PT $1,600; stock fell from $2,000 to $1,200
bullets.body: Argus Research upgraded SanDisk to Buy with a $1,600 price target. SNDK has fallen ~40% from its $2,000 high amid memory sector volatility. The weekly memory rundown showed mixed results and guidance from SanDisk and Western Digital vs. elevated expectations.

bullets.title: COHR/LITE: Optical names pulling back after 70%+ runs; CLSA prefers LITE
bullets.body: Coherent experienced reversion after a >70% rally in 7 days following the optical-memory spread. LITE also pulled back on profit-taking, insider selling, and high valuation. CLSA analyst Briley prefers LITE over COHR in optical components, estimating COHR's annual 3D sensing run-rate below $100M. Wolfe Research hosting LITE earnings callback Aug 11 and COHR callback Aug 12.

bullets.title: APP: Citi Buy; Week 32 eCommerce store count grows 0.7% to 10,908; Jefferies hosts expert call Aug 17
bullets.body: AppLovin's eCommerce client base reached 10,908 stores as of Week 32 (up 0.7% WoW), with US stores at 5,064 (+0.5%). 3Q26 QTD weekly store growth averaging 1.0%, implying ~11.1K average. Jefferies hosts expert call Aug 17 with DIFF Eyewear discussing ROAS vs. Meta/Google. Jefferies maintains Buy/$550 PT.

bullets.title: SPOT/UBER: GS desk flags follow-through buying; MS intern survey shows SPOT at 71% music streaming share
bullets.body: Goldman sales desk notes SPOT up ~5% on healthy bull/bear balance post-2Q earnings and UBER up ~20% in two weeks re-testing 200-dma. Morgan Stanley 2026 intern survey shows Spotify extending lead as most popular music streaming service at 71% (up from 69%), beating Apple Music at 28%; Netflix dropped from #1 to #3 in video streaming behind YouTube (22%) and others.

bullets.title: HPE: Upgraded to Overweight at Morgan Stanley; breaks to 52-week high above $30
bullets.body: HPE was upgraded to Overweight at Morgan Stanley on improved enterprise storage spending trends and broke out to a 52-week high above $30 for the first time in ~15 months.

bullets.title: GOOGL: YouTube doubles monetization watch-hour threshold; $200B CapEx guiding FCF negative
bullets.body: YouTube raised its minimum watch-hour requirement to 10M (from 5M) for creator monetization. Alphabet is guiding to ~$200B in CapEx for 2026 (25% of total hyperscaler spend), with FCF turning negative at -$5B in Q2 and management expecting spend to rise into 2027. Google also added AI/agentic capabilities to Google Ads and Analytics. Appeals court allowed addiction lawsuits against Google (and Meta) to proceed.

bullets.title: CEVA: UBS maintains Buy/$48 PT; new major US AI deal and Apple handset ramp intact for C27
bullets.body: UBS keeps Buy on CEVA with $48 PT (44x 2028E P/E on $1.11 EPS). Key catalysts: new AI licensing partnership with major US AI company described as most strategically significant in CEVA history, materially larger than typical $1-2MM deals; Apple premium-tier ramp expected to contribute ~$7-10MM royalty revenue in C27 at ~$0.075/device; FY26 revenue growth guidance raised to 13-15%. AI contributes ~20% of revenues now with strong royalty growth expected from 2027.

bullets.title: WBD: Upgraded to Buy at Freedom Broker with $31 PT; PSKY offers 3-year theatrical exclusivity
bullets.body: Warner Bros. Discovery was upgraded to Buy from Hold at Freedom Broker with a $31 price target (14% upside from $27.08). Separately, PSKY offered 3-year contracts guaranteeing 45-day theatrical exclusivity and 90-day no-streaming as part of a potential WBD acquisition bid, pledging 30 films/year in theaters.

bullets.title: HD/LOW: UBS bullish into 2Q; models $4.84/share for HD and $4.24 for LOW; deferred demand ~$74B
bullets.body: UBS expects 2Q results to build confidence in home improvement recovery. HD modeled at 2Q EPS $4.84 (cons $4.73) and LOW at $4.24 (in line), with HD targeting $400M pro cross-selling run-rate by end of 2026. UBS estimates ~$74B in deferred discretionary home improvement demand. HD trades ~22x CY27 EPS, LOW ~17x—UBS views as undemanding given business quality.

bullets.title: CSCO: F4Q26 earnings preview—Street at $16.82B revenue, $1.17 EPS; AI orders $9B FY26
bullets.body: Cisco reports with Street expecting F4Q26 revenue of $16.82B and non-GAAP EPS of $1.17. Investors focused on AI orders trajectory ($9B FY26 target), security segment recovery (weak F1Q-F3Q on cloud shift), and whether 34% operating margin holds in FY27. Wolfe Research hosting management meetings at ECOC 2026 Sept 21-22.

bullets.title: AMAT: F3Q26 earnings preview Aug 13—Street at $9.0B revenue; DRAM/packaging to drive >80% of WFE growth
bullets.body: Applied Materials reports F3Q26 on August 13. Street consensus is $9.0B revenue (+0.6% above guidance midpoint) and EPS of $3.40. DRAM and advanced packaging expected to drive over 80% of wafer fab equipment growth in CY26, with WFE spending projected to double from CY23 to CY27.
